runs.driving_observable: HELD AT AMBER — de-escalation candidate, not yet de-escalated. The armed catalyst fired and did NOT produce the RED marker: the compound test was a turnover spike ON FALLING price, and the session delivered a turnover spike on RISING price (2.0-2.1x average volume, close +6.14%). The 'break below the recent ~$108-111 lows on elevated volume' clause was touched intraday ($105.11, a new all-time low) but reversed within the session to close near the high — a supply test met by demand, which is the opposite of a run. Two reasons this is not yet GREEN. (1) The de-escalation clause requires 'modest REALIZED selling', and realized selling is unobservable today: Form 4s lag up to two business days, so no insider-disposition data exists yet for 08-06. Absent that, a GREEN call would rest on price action alone. (2) The structural run capacity rose sharply — free float went 4.9% -> 11.8% of shares outstanding — and only the first 20% tranche is out, with further staggered tranches through the 2026-12-08 full expiry. The mechanism is better-capitalized against a run than yesterday in sentiment terms and materially worse in structural terms.

fire_sales.driving_observable: HELD AT AMBER — unchanged rating, materially better-specified basis. The AMBER condition is untouched: price remains below the $135 offer, so stock-settled obligations are not covered with headroom. What changed is that the two "unquantified null" holes flagged since 08-05 have been worked from primary filings, and they resolve in opposite directions. The PLEDGE channel is now ruled out: only 2,618,530 Class A shares are disclosed as pledged for personal indebtedness (Musk 237,530, Nosek 2,381,000) = 0.0199% of shares outstanding, 0.168% of float, ~1% of one session's volume. Private loan trigger LEVELS are still undisclosed and always will be — they live in unfiled agreements — but that no longer gates the rating, because the maximum supply from total foreclosure is immaterial at any trigger price. The OBLIGATION structure is confirmed worse than recorded: the Cursor consideration is a fixed $60B of value divided by a 7-day VWAP with NO COLLAR (Section 2.05 adjusts only for recapitalisation events), so dilution scales as 1/P without bound — 522.1M shares at the $114.92 close versus 444.4M at the offer, and 800.0M at $75; and the $10B / $4B termination fees became payable ONLY IN CASH once SPCX became a Public Parent (Section 11.04(d)), removing the stock-settlement election a private issuer would have had. No forced event is visible: no margin call, no pledged-share liquidation, no renegotiation or collapse. RED still requires a visible forced event, and the pledge finding makes one materially less likely from that channel. REFINEMENT, same rating: the $10B cash exposure is 85% a deferred services fee under the unfiled Compute Agreement and only 15% a termination fee, and it has a CONDITIONAL ESCAPE HATCH that cannot be read from public documents. Section 10.01(c)(iv) lets SPCX terminate the merger if it terminates the Compute Agreement for a "Specified Material Breach" under Annex A thereto, and Section 11.04(c) makes the $10B payable ONLY IF SPCX has not terminated, and is not entitled to terminate, on that ground. The Compute Agreement is NOT filed — the S-1's material contracts are the indemnification form, the ESPP, two equity plans, two Class B RSA agreements, a License Purchase Agreement and a Bridge Loan Credit Agreement, with no compute or option agreement among them — so Annex A and Section 6.2(b) are unavailable permanently, exactly as the pledge trigger levels are. Consequence for this mechanism: the largest single cash exposure is BOUNDED ABOVE at $10B but NOT DETERMINABLE BELOW, and the text that determines it is one no outside party can read. That is a second structural observability limit of the same kind as the pledge levels, and it should be recorded as such rather than carried as a pending research item.

observables.cursor_acq_stock_component: ~$60B all-stock, consideration formula now filing-verified (EX-10.1 Section 1.01): Exchange Ratio = Company Implied Per Share Value / Parent Share Price, where Company Implied Per Share Value = a FIXED $60,000,000,000 equity value divided by Anysphere's fully diluted capitalisation, and Parent Share Price = the volume-weighted average closing price over the 7 consecutive trading days ending the trading day immediately preceding Closing. NO COLLAR: Section 2.05 adjusts only for reclassification, split, recap and stock-dividend events, with no floor, ceiling or price-based walk-away. Issuance therefore scales as 1/P without bound — 444.4M shares at $135, 522.1M at $114.92, 570.8M at $105.11, 666.7M at $90, 800.0M at $75 (3.37% / 3.96% / 4.33% / 5.06% / 6.07% of shares outstanding); each 10% decline issues 11.1% more stock. Shares issued carry a Lock-Up Period (Letter of Transmittal; Exhibit D IPO Lock-Up Agreement), so they do not enter float at closing. Expected close Q3 2026 under antitrust scrutiny. Termination fees $10B (Total Fee) / $4B (Regulatory Total Fee), never both (11.04(e)), and payable ONLY IN CASH now that Parent is public (11.04(d)); the $10B fee is further conditioned on the separate SPCX-Anysphere Compute Agreement. FEE STRUCTURE REFINED FROM PRIMARY FILINGS — the $10B is mostly NOT a break fee. Merger agreement Section 11.04(f), tracking Section 6.2(b) of the Compute Agreement, splits it 15/85, and the 424B4 states the split in plain numbers: $1.5B termination fee under the option/merger agreement PLUS $8.5B deferred services fee under the separate Compute Agreement. The same 15/85 split applies to the $4B regulatory fee ($0.6B + $3.4B). These are different legal animals: a break fee is liquidated damages on a transaction that did not happen; a deferred services fee is consideration under a commercial contract that did. Deal history also corrected: the acquisition was never a commitment but a CALL OPTION dated 2026-04-19, exercisable in the 30-day window following the earlier of (i) seven trading days after IPO completion and (ii) 2026-09-30, at SPCX's sole discretion with board approval, with Cursor under exclusivity; the 10-Q carries its initial fair value at ZERO. SPCX exercised in June and signed the merger agreement 06-16. Cash-only settlement confirmed from a second document: the 424B4 says the fees are "payable in cash (or Class A common stock, if this offering has not been consummated at the time the fees become payable)" — the IPO closed 06-12, so the stock election lapsed.
observables.valor_equipment_lease_exposure: Valor-linked compute SPV ~$20B (~$7.5B equity + ~$12.5B debt) to acquire Nvidia chips, with an xAI/SPCX option to acquire the hardware at lease end; Nvidia ~$2B equity into the SPV (risk shifted toward Valor).
observables.margin_lending_against_spcx: No margin lending against SPCX stock disclosed at company level, and no margin loan or margin account facility appears in the 424B4 or the Q2 10-Q. Company secured debt is asset-backed rather than stock-backed: $1.5B ABL revolver collateralised by inventory and equipment; other equipment financings at ~5.3-5.5%; plus a facility collateralised by securities held in xAI's custodial account (related-party, worth separate tracking). Insider-level borrowing is visible only through the pledge footnotes above; the loans themselves are not filed.
observables.insider_pledged_shares: 2,618,530 Class A shares pledged as security for personal indebtedness, per 424B4 beneficial-ownership footnotes (1) and (7): Musk 237,530 (0.028% of his ~849.5M Class A); Nosek 2,381,000 (7.22% of his 32.99M). Total = 0.0199% of 13,181,779,945 shares outstanding, 0.168% of post-unlock float, ~1.07% of the 08-06 session volume, ~$300.9M at $114.92. Class B auto-converts to Class A on any pledge or hypothecation, penalising the supervoting holders for pledging. Lock-up exception (xv) permits a third-party pledgee to enforce by selling lock-up securities, so these shares escape the lockup on foreclosure — bounded by the same 2.6M.

observables.convertible_or_stock_settled_instruments: The Cursor consideration remains the principal stock-settled obligation and is uncollared, so a below-offer price raises the issuance count with no contractual floor. Note the termination fees are NOT stock-settled for a public SPCX — Section 11.04(d) makes them cash-only, so the $10B/$4B exposure is a hard cash claim rather than an issuance. Scope check completed on other pending stock-settled deals: the MESH OPTICAL merger (May 2026, optical transceivers) is a FIXED 3.8M-share consideration — not value-based, no VWAP, no collar exposure — with a cash election of up to $2.5M each for Class B holders, and it CLOSED 2026-07-06. ~$437M at $114.92, 0.03% of shares outstanding. Ruled out as a second uncollared obligation; the Cursor consideration remains the only one.

observables.counterparty_web_status: CORRECTED — xAI IS NOT A COUNTERPARTY, IT IS INSIDE SPCX. SpaceX acquired X.AI Holdings Corp. effective 2026-02-02 (the "xAI Merger"); xAI had itself acquired X Holdings effective 2025-03-28. Both were common-control transactions and the financials are retrospectively recast (424B4, Basis of Presentation). The prospectus defines the AI segment as the business "acquired in connection with our acquisition of xAI in February 2026… includes our AI compute, Grok, and X". Every prior entry treating xAI as an external node checked for operational distress was wrong: xAI stress is DIRECT SEGMENT EXPOSURE, not contagion. The distinction is load-bearing in a Brunnermeier-Reis frame — network transmission has lags and possible circuit-breakers, balance-sheet exposure has neither. Also newly recorded: the same filing shows a five-for-one stock split effective 2026-05-04, which is why all share figures are retroactively adjusted. REVISED WEB: (i) Cursor/Anysphere — dual-role, both a compute counterparty since 2026-04-19 and the pending acquisition target, closing expected Q3 2026 under antitrust scrutiny; (ii) the Valor SPV — ALSO dual-role, since the Valor entities hold ~503.4M shares (7.3% pre-offering) through Antonio J. Gracias, who is a director, making the compute-SPV counterparty simultaneously a large shareholder and board-connected; (iii) Anthropic as a compute customer; (iv) Mesh Optical, acquired and closed 2026-07-06, now internal. No node is in visible operational distress. The genuine external web is therefore SMALLER than previously recorded, and two of its three remaining nodes are dual-role — which concentrates rather than diversifies the exposure.
